subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename workspace files as part of the core bootstrap context contract, and should that contract stay global, become exact-session scoped, or move into a broader context API?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but broadening startup context injection creates a public config and prompt-surface contract under repository policy that treats config/session-state changes as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
options.body: Allow explicit in-workspace custom basenames through `bootstrap-extra-files` after the linked PR or a replacement is repaired, documented, and tested against path guards, budgets, and session filtering.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames Only
options.body: Decline arbitrary workspace-file injection for now and direct users to first-class workspace filenames or documented conventions instead.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context Design
options.body: Keep this issue open only as design input if maintainers want a larger context or capability API instead of raw configured files.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
recommendation.body: Allow explicit in-workspace custom basenames through `bootstrap-extra-files` after the linked PR or a replacement is repaired, documented, and tested against path guards, budgets, and session filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available owner from the history for the original hook merge and the boundary-safe bootstrap read contract.
